To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of leaf litter to the ground in a coniferous plantation increased the abundance of a habitat generalist species (Pterosichus oblongo-punctatus) and altered the species composition of carabid assemblages.

(1) the addition of leaf litter to a conifer plantation resulted in a significant change of the carabid assemblage; (2) the most numerous carabid species (Pter. oblongopunctatatus) was more abundant in the litter plots, while there were no significant changes for other species; (3) the carabid catch in the litter plots was significantly higher during both years, but the species richness, abundance and Shannon diversity were similar between the two
the addition of leaf litter increased the number of individuals of P. oblongopunctata, but did not influence the number of other species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of leaf litter addition on carabid assemblages in a conifer plantation.
the effects of leaf-litter manipulation on ground-dwelling beetles in a conifer plantation.
the effect of leaf litter on carabid assemblages in a managed forest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

leaf-litter addition in a conifer plantation increased the abundance of a habitat specialist carabid species and the habitat heterogeneity, but it did not significantly change the diversity of the carabid fauna in this study.
carabid species richness, diversity and abundance were positively affected by leaf-litter addition, and the most frequently obtained species were significantly more abundant in leaf-litter plots.
the effect of the leaf-litter addition was not significant for the majority of the species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of leaf litter in homogeneous plantations can increase the abundance and diversity of ground-dwelling carabids.
leaf-litter addition in a conifer plantation increased the diversity of carabid assemblages.
carabids responded to the leaf-litter addition by increasing the abundance and species richness of some species and by changing the composition of the community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of leaf-litter can be an effective way to improve habitat heterogeneity in conifer plantations, and thus to enhance the diversity of carabids and other ground-dwelling invertebrates.
adding litter in a forest plantation is a simple, effective, and inexpensive way to increase the diversity and richness of carabids.
the effects of habitat manipulation are species-specific.
